paper_title: dKV-Cache The Cache for Diffusion Language Models
caption: Impact of batch size on decoding speed. Evaluated on LLaDA with a single NVIDIA H20; prefill length fixed at 100 tokens.
model_annotation: This line chart illustrates the impact of batch size on decoding speed across different cache configurations for diffusion language models, with performance measured in tokens per second (Token/s) on the y-axis and batch size on the x-axis, which ranges from 0 to 120 and is marked at regular intervals of 20. The y-axis spans from 0 to 225 Token/s, also marked at regular intervals of 25. Four distinct lines represent different cache configurations: a solid blue line labeled 'L = 16', a solid dark blue line labeled 'dKV-Cache-Decode', a solid red line labeled 'L = 64', and a solid dark gray line labeled 'Origin'. The 'L = 16' line starts at approximately 25 Token/s and rises sharply to 173.17 Token/s at batch size 40, then continues to increase more gradually to 183.28 Token/s at batch size 120. The 'dKV-Cache-Decode' line begins at approximately 25 Token/s and increases steadily to 202.31 Token/s at batch size 120. The 'L = 64' line starts near 25 Token/s, rises to 119.55 Token/s at batch size 40, and then plateaus slightly to 130.58 Token/s at batch size 120. The 'Origin' line begins at approximately 25 Token/s and remains nearly flat throughout, reaching 35.42 Token/s at batch size 120. All lines are marked with circular data points, and the 'dKV-Cache-Decode' line is accompanied by a legend indicating its association with the dark blue line.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the impact of batch size on decoding speed, measured in tokens per second (Token/s), for four different model sizes (L = 16, L = 32, L = 64, L = 128) and two decoding methods (dKV-Cache-Decode and Origin). The x-axis represents Batch Size, ranging from 0 to 120, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The y-axis represents Token/s, ranging from 0 to 225, with tick marks at intervals of 25. The plot includes four lines for each model size: for L = 16, a light gray line with circle markers, a blue line with triangle markers, and a red line with square markers; for L = 32, a dark blue line with diamond markers; for L = 64, a dashed dark blue line with triangle markers; and for L = 128, a dashed dark blue line with square markers. The dKV-Cache-Decode method is shown with a solid dark blue line with diamond markers, while the Origin method is shown with a dashed dark blue line with square markers. The lines show that decoding speed generally increases with batch size for all configurations, with the L = 128 model achieving the highest speeds (up to 202.31 Token/s at batch size 120) and the L = 16 model achieving the lowest speeds (up to 173.17 Token/s at batch size 120). The dKV-Cache-Decode method consistently outperforms the Origin method across all batch sizes and model sizes.
